title.value: Learning Improvised Chatbots from Adversarial Modifications of Natural Language Feedback
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Learning Improvised Chatbots from Adversarial Modifications of Natural Language Feedback

analysis.description: The paper proposes a new method for improving chatbot performance by transforming noisy user feedback into plausible responses using a generative adversarial model called F EED 2R ESP. The model improves upon previous attempts by converting feedback into useful training samples without needing full supervision, demonstrating significant improvements particularly when integrated with strong chatbot models.

type.justification: The paper provides experimental results showing the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving chatbot performance.
type.quote: We show that augmenting original training data with these modified feedback responses improves the original chatbot performance from 69.94% to 75.96% in ranking correct responses on the P ERSONA C HAT dataset.

name.justification: The paper focuses on chatbot performance and conversation handling, which falls under the NLP domain.
name.quote: We use BART encoder-decoder initialized with pretrained weights as our generator since its denoising objective helps in copying from the input while also producing realistic sentences (Lewis et al., 2019).

name.justification: The focus of the paper is on improving chatbot performance via feedback handling.
name.quote: We show that augmenting original training data with these modified feedback responses improves the original chatbot performance.

name.justification: F EED 2R ESP is the main model proposed in this paper for converting feedback into natural responses.
name.quote: We introduce F EED 2R ESP , a text style transfer system that converts feedback to natural responses without full supervision.

is_contributed.justification: F EED 2R ESP is the novel contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: We introduce F EED 2R ESP, a text style transfer system.

is_executed.justification: There is no specific mention of execution on a particular hardware (GPU or CPU).

is_compared.justification: F EED 2R ESP's performance is compared against other feedback handling techniques.
is_compared.quote: Naive and heuristic use of feedback results in marginal improvement or hurts performance, whereas F EED 2R ESP modified feedback gives large improvements.
